The mass spectrometry data shows:
- Base peak (100% intensity) at m/z = 179.09462866255998
- This is likely the molecular ion [M+H]+ or [M-H]- depending on ionization mode

Since ESI (Electrospray Ionization) was used, the most common ion in positive mode is [M+H]+. So the molecular weight would be approximately 179.09463 - 1.00783 = 178.08680 Da.

Let me analyze the isotope pattern:
- m/z 179.09463 (100%)
- m/z 180.09783 (11.41%) - this is M+1 isotope
- m/z 181.10013 (1.00%) - this is M+2 isotope

The M+1 peak at ~11.4% suggests significant carbon content (each carbon contributes ~1.1% to M+1).
The M+2 peak at ~1% is relatively small, suggesting no chlorine, bromine, or sulfur (which would show much larger M+2 peaks).

For a molecular weight around 178 Da with ~11.4% M+1:
- Number of carbons ≈ 11.4 / 1.1 ≈ 10-11 carbons

Let me consider possible formulas around 178 Da:
- C10H10O3: 10(12.011) + 10(1.008) + 3(15.999) = 178.063 Da
- C11H14O2: 11(12.011) + 14(1.008) + 2(15.999) = 178.099 Da
- C9H10O4: 9(12.011) + 10(1.008) + 4(15.999) = 178.063 Da

The exact mass of 178.08680 is closest to C10H10O3 (178.0630) or C11H14O2 (178.0994).

Actually, let me recalculate more precisely:
- C10H10O3 = 178.06299 Da
- C11H14O2 = 178.09938 Da
- C9H10O4 = 178.05791 Da

The observed m/z of 179.09463 (assuming [M+H]+) gives M = 178.08680 Da.

C11H14O2 = 178.09938 Da is very close!

Let me verify the isotope pattern for C11H14O2:
- 11 carbons would give M+1 ≈ 11 × 1.1% = 12.1% (close to observed 11.4%)
- 2 oxygens would give M+2 ≈ 2 × 0.2% = 0.4% (close to observed 1.0%)

This matches well! The formula is likely C11H14O2.
